response.sql:
WITH equip_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    equipref,
    AVG(humepct) as equip_avg
  FROM scanenvironment
  WHERE humepct IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY equipref
),
equip_avg_overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(equip_avg) as overall_avg
  FROM equip_avgs
),
filtered_equips AS (
  SELECT 
    ea.equipref,
    ea.equip_avg,
    eo.overall_avg
  FROM equip_avgs ea
  CROSS JOIN equip_avg_overall eo
  WHERE eo.overall_avg IS NOT NULL
    AND ea.equip_avg > eo.overall_avg
),
kept_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(equip_avg) as kept_mean
  FROM filtered_equips
)
SELECT 
  fe.equipref,
  fe.equip_avg,
  fe.equip_avg - fe.overall_avg as diff_from_overall,
  fe.equip_avg - ka.kept_mean as diff_from_kept_mean
FROM filtered_equips fe
CROSS JOIN kept_avg ka
WHERE ka.kept_mean IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 
  CASE WHEN fe.equip_avg - ka.kept_mean IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  fe.equip_avg - ka.kept_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "The average of all equipment averages" refers to the average of equipment-specific averages (AVG(equip_avg) for all equipment with non-NULL humepct readings), not the overall average of all humepct values. This interpretation aligns with the literal phrasing 'average of ... averages'.

alternatives.interpretation: "The average of all equipment averages" could instead mean the overall average of all humepct values across all rows (AVG(humepct)), where equipment with insufficient data are excluded. This would give different filtered equipment and rankings.
